mechanisms.name: Exact handle or invite discovery
notes: The client does not upload or privately test its address book; a user supplies an exact handle, QR code, invite link, or equivalent discovery token.
The service may learn the exact queried handle unless another transport/privacy profile conceals it.
The profile minimizes address-book exposure rather than hiding each explicit lookup.

mechanisms.name: RFC 9497 VOPRF private membership discovery
notes: The server evaluates blinded normalized identifiers and learns neither client inputs nor VOPRF outputs from the VOPRF execution.
The client verifies the VOPRF proof against a pinned public key for the selected directory epoch.
Directory membership is represented by authenticated/versioned pseudorandom tags derived from VOPRF outputs.
Online evaluation limits are required because low-entropy identifier spaces remain enumerable by an authorized client.

mechanisms.name: Attested confidential-compute contact intersection
notes: The client remotely attests the confidential-compute instance before sending encrypted contact identifiers.
Only measured code inside the trusted execution boundary receives plaintext query identifiers.
The untrusted host/service receives only ciphertext, coarse request metadata, and the permitted result shape.
Security depends on the selected TEE, attestation chain, measured implementation, and declared side-channel model.
